author: Vitor
notes: Possible to pre-calculate for every single possible value.
aiExplanation: This code solves a two-player game where players take turns removing a **perfect square** number of stones (1, 4, 9, 16, ...) from a pile, and the player who can't move loses. It uses **dynamic programming** to precompute, for every pile size up to `100,000`, whether the player whose turn it is can force a win. The array `res` holds these answers: `res[0]` is `false` (no stones left means the current player loses) and `res[1]` is `true` (take the single stone and win). For each pile size `i`, the inner loop tries every possible move `j * j` and checks the position it leaves behind — if any move lands the opponent in a **losing** position (`!res[i - j * j]`), then the current player **can win**, so `res[i]` is set to `true`. Because all of this work happens once at module load, the actual `winnerSquareGame` function is just an instant **array lookup**: `return res[n]`.
